source_review.notes: Checked official Google SRE monitoring, troubleshooting, reliability-testing, and postmortem guidance; current Apache Spark, Apache Flink, and Apache Beam operational documentation; current Prometheus histogram guidance; and the NIST/SEMATECH comparison handbook. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific metrics and mechanisms are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed eligible/admitted/start/durable timestamps, end-to-end and lifecycle durations, DAG critical path, correct work, observation interval, throughput, resource busy time/utilization/demand, backlog, event-time latency, cost, and efficiency notation.
Checked dimensional consistency for elapsed time, useful work/time, busy time/completion, utilization, and useful work/cost.
Checked explicit warning that lifecycle components add only when mutually exclusive and that parallel resource busy times can overlap/exceed wall time.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Rates, percentiles, costs, and durations retain their workload population, time interval, resource scope, and completion boundary.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 2,000 seconds end-to-end plus a 2,000-second sum across mutually exclusive lifecycle states.
Recomputed four billion correct records over 2,000 seconds as 2.000 million records/s useful throughput and execution slack as 1,620 minus 1,500 = 120 seconds.
Recomputed a predicted 120-second reduction as 1,880 seconds candidate elapsed time and 1.064 times predicted speedup.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture validates accounting arithmetic; the predicted improvement remains a hypothesis requiring paired representative trials, correct output, guardrails, and rollback.

evidence: Verified end-to-end elapsed time is durable-valid minus eligible time and mutually exclusive lifecycle states may reconcile to it.
Verified any DAG execution is bounded below by its maximum precedence-path sum while shortening noncritical parallel work need not reduce completion.
Derived utilization equals throughput times service demand from aligned busy-time, completion, and observation-window definitions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The critical-path and service-demand relations are diagnostic constraints, not proof that any proposed intervention attains its predicted effect.

evidence: Reviewed empty/tiny/large/skewed workloads, cold/warm caches, late/null/duplicate data, wrong outputs, asynchronous commits, and unrepresentative review windows.
Reviewed clock skew, sampled/missing metrics, overlapping timers, censored/failed tasks, retries/speculation, worker/resource skew, adaptive plans, and shared load.
Reviewed streaming backlog, checkpoint/state growth, storage/network/request/dependency limits, quota exhaustion, worker/coordinator failure, recovery, cost, and security.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Batch, streaming, incident, benchmark, recovery, capacity, and cost cohorts are kept distinct while joined through stable evidence identities.

evidence: Traced workload from eligibility/admission through plans, tasks, retries, state/checkpoints, storage/shuffle, durable commit, catalog publication, validation, and downstream visibility.
Checked input/output conservation across offered, accepted, queued, attempted, retried, failed, expired-by-policy, and correctly committed work.
Checked every recommendation against semantics, retry/idempotency, ordering/windows, state, security, retention, recovery, capacity, cost, owner, experiment, guardrail, and rollback.
invariant_checking.notes: Performance evidence is ineligible until the correctness and durability oracle passes for the same workload and system boundary.

evidence: Reviewed critical-path lower-bound reasoning and the distinction between parallel task/resource work and elapsed time.
Reviewed service-demand accounting as a cross-check for aligned observations and its limits when workload or capacity changes.
Reviewed counterfactual falsification chain from scoped symptom/evidence through mechanism, intervention, measurable prediction, verification, and rollback.
proof_review.notes: Correlations become causal findings only with alternatives, predicted evidence changes, controlled discrimination where feasible, confidence, and limitations.

evidence: Audited end-to-end review, review contract, useful work, critical path, service center, bottleneck, finding, recommendation, capacity envelope, counterfactual, reproducibility, and residual-risk terminology.
Confirmed symptoms versus causes, observation versus inference, high utilization versus binding constraint, stage duration versus critical path, and submitted versus committed work remain distinct.
Confirmed local speedup, predicted effect, controlled benchmark result, production canary, and realized outcome are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The review chain makes each conclusion traceable from objective and workload through evidence and verification.

evidence: Reviewed objective/SLO, workload/output oracle, lifecycle events, input/output identity, plans, tasks/partitions/keys/attempts/workers, and resource/dependency evidence.
Reviewed CPU/memory/GC/spill, storage/network/shuffle/requests, queues/backlog/watermarks, state/checkpoints, retries/failures/recovery, topology/configuration/version, and cost.
Confirmed evidence is segmented by execution, stage/operator, task/partition/key, attempt/worker/resource, cache/load/failure cohort, percentile, and time.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Dashboard screenshots, averages, precomputed worker percentiles, one warm run, or missing telemetry are not mislabeled as complete causal evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed charter/objectives, workload and system boundaries, evidence/lifecycle/graph reconstruction, distributions, service centers, memory/serialization, data movement/storage, streaming, failure/recovery, capacity/cost, causal findings, interventions, verification, communication, and outcome feedback.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable review contracts, evidence maps, correctness gates, timelines/critical paths, counterfactual findings, ranked recommendations, representative paired experiments, canaries, guardrails, rollback, ownership, residual risk, and expiry triggers. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified capstone progression from objectives and boundaries through cross-layer reconstruction, diagnosis, causal findings, intervention, and follow-through. Ten examples and five answered exercises integrate lifecycle arithmetic, critical paths, service centers, streaming, retries, cost, experiments, and final decision packages.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Google/Spark/Flink/Beam/Prometheus/NIST maintainer, distributed-data/runtime/storage/network/platform/SRE/performance/statistics/security/economics specialist, production operator, business owner, downstream consumer, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
